question: Assume the JTB definition of Knowledge, which suggests that "Knowledge is a Justified True Belief". If our only available epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief, what are the two problems JTB runs into? Ignore Gettier problems.

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The two problems are the redundancy/collapse of the justification condition and the inaccessibility of the truth condition. If the only epistemic states available are Knowledge and Belief, then “justification” must be either a belief or a piece of knowledge. If it is merely belief, then a true belief plus another belief that it is justified is still just true belief, so the justification clause adds nothing and JTB collapses into true belief. If it is knowledge, then the definition becomes uninformative because it uses knowledge to explain knowledge. Separately, truth is not itself an epistemic state: from the inside, a true belief and a false belief can be equally believed and equally justified, so the truth condition cannot be recognized or guaranteed by either Knowledge or Belief. Thus JTB faces the problem that justification is either redundant or presupposed, and the problem that truth remains epistemically inaccessible.

1.text:
Under JTB you have four logically distinct combinations of truth value and
justification

* T & J  = Knowledge
* T & ~J = true belief without warrant
* ~T & J = justified false belief
* ~T & ~J = unjustified false belief

If the taxonomy you are allowed to use is only

K = Justified True Belief
B = everything else

then the three non-knowledge cells are all mapped onto the single state B.
Justification is therefore invisible outside of K.

* Justified false belief. A belief can be properly based, rationally held,
evidentially supported and yet false. On JTB it is not knowledge because
the truth condition fails, but with only K/B at your disposal it is
indistinguishable from an irrational false belief. The epistemic value of
justification is lost for falsehoods.

* Unjustified true belief. A belief can be true but held by luck, guess,
coincidence or on no warrant at all. On JTB it is not knowledge because the
justification condition fails, but with only K/B at your disposal it is
indistinguishable from a justified false belief. The epistemic defect of
lack of warrant is lost for truths.

That is the classic pre-Gettier collapse that JTB produces under a binary
K/B ontology: justified false belief and unjustified true belief are both
mere Belief, and justified false belief and unjustified false belief are
also both mere Belief. Justification can only be registered in the one
cell T&J = Knowledge, so the gradations of rationality that JTB is meant to
capture are erased outside of knowledge.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only the two tags Knowledge and Belief you have no way to keep justification and truth separate inside the Belief box.

On JTB

* K(p) iff J(p) & T(p) & B(p)
* B(p) is the remainder.

So with a binary taxonomy every p is either K or B and K entails B.

That forces two different epistemically heterogeneous groups into the same B tag.

1. Justification without truth. A Justified False Belief J(p) & ~T(p) & B(p).
It is epistemically good in the justification dimension and for that reason it is in every relevant sense knowledge-like, but it is not K because it is not true. With only K / B available it can only be filed as B, i.e. as mere belief. Belief therefore has to contain justified beliefs as well as unjustified beliefs.

2. Truth without justification. An Unjustified True Belief ~J(p) & T(p) & B(p).
It is epistemically good in the truth dimension and for that reason it is truth-like, but it is not K because it is not justified. With only K / B available it can only be filed as B, i.e. as mere belief. Belief therefore has to contain true beliefs as well as false beliefs.

In other words Belief on a JTB binary taxonomy is the disjunction
B = J & ~T  ∨  ~J & T  ∨  ~J & ~T
justified false belief, unjustified true belief and unjustified false belief are all one and the same epistemic state. The state Belief is therefore heterogeneous and it loses the independent information carried by justification and by truth. Knowledge is a proper sub-species of belief, K ⊂ B, so a known proposition is double tagged as both K and B, while epistemically distinct non-knowledge cases are forced to share the same B label. That is the justification-mismatch and the truth-mismatch that a two-state JTB taxonomy cannot accommodate, independently of Gettier.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: JTB gives you only one factive good state and one non-factive catch-all state.

On the JTB taxonomy

* K p  =  B p & J p & T p
* B p  =  not K p

so any proposition that fails either T or J is just “B”. With only the two
labels Knowledge and Belief in the ontology that coarse-graining costs you
independent tracking of justification and of truth.

* The false-but-justified problem. A belief can be fully justified and still
false. On JTB that state is not K p because T p fails, so it is simply B p.
It is therefore ontologically indistinguishable from an unjustified, baseless
false belief. You have no epistemic room for “well supported false belief’’
as a distinct epistemic value from “mere false belief”. In effect justified
false belief is collapsed into unqualified belief.

* The true-but-unjustified problem. A belief can be true for contingent,
luck-based reasons and be completely unjustified. On JTB that state is not K p
because J p fails, so it is simply B p. It is therefore ontologically
indistinguishable from a false belief, and from a justified false belief.
You have no epistemic room for “lucky true belief’’ as a distinct epistemic
value from “bad belief’’.

Hence with the two-state inventory Knowledge / Belief you cannot keep
justification and truth as independent epistemic goods. Justification is
only visible where it coincides with truth, and truth is only epistemically
marked where it coincides with justification. That is why the traditional
non-Gettier criticism is that JTB forces a collapse of

* justified false belief → belief, and
* true but unjustified belief → belief,

so the taxonomy cannot differentiate epistemically good-but-false belief
from bad false belief, nor lucky true belief from bad belief. The familiar
lottery / preface type phenomena are the intuitive expression of the same
coarseness.

5.text:
With the tripartite analysis truth and justification give you four logical
positions

* JT = justified true belief
* JF = justified false belief
* UT = unjustified true belief
* UF = unjustified false belief

On JTB JT is knowledge and everything else is, by stipulation, just
belief. The name `belief' is therefore doing the work of three
different epistemic positions.

* JF. A justified false belief is epistemically good in the only sense
JTB cares about, it is justified, and for the subject it is
subjectively indistinguishable from a case of knowledge. The subject
is in a state of justified belief, he believes p, he takes p to be
justified, and he has no internal way of telling that p is in fact
false. On a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy JF has to be called mere
belief. Belief is therefore heterogenous: it contains both
epistemically defective false beliefs and epistemically respectable
false beliefs, and knowledge is internally indistinguishable from a
justified false belief.

That is the classic need for a state of justified belief distinct from
knowledge. If you do not have a justified-belief state the JTB
machine makes the good false belief look like a bad false belief.

* UT. A true belief which is not justified is true but unendorsed. It
is the paradigm lucky or accidental true belief. On a
Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy UT also has to be called mere belief.
Belief is therefore again heterogenous: it contains false beliefs,
both justified and unjustified, and also true beliefs which happen to
be true without warrant. Knowledge is thus externally indistinguishable
from an unjustified true belief so far as truth goes, and the
difference between a lucky true belief and a plain false belief is
lost in the single category `belief'.

In the usual 2 × 2 picture that is just the two non-knowledge cells
that JTB is forced to lump together under the single label `belief'.
It is this lumping which makes justification have to be cashed out in
terms of other beliefs. With only Knowledge and Belief as states a
justification for a belief can only be a further belief, which is
itself either knowledge = JT or mere belief. That is the familiar
regress / circularity problem for the justification condition: a
justified belief is justified by beliefs, those beliefs need
justification, etc., with no distinct justified-belief state in which
the regress can stop. Gettier aside that is the cost of trying to make
knowledge a species of belief with only the truth and justification
marks to separate them.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about the cost of JTB under a binary K/B ontology, Gettier excluded.

Core 2x2: JT = Knowledge; JF = justified false belief; UT = unjustified true belief; UF = unjustified false belief. With only Knowledge and Belief as labels, K = JT, B = not K = JF ∨ UT ∨ UF. Belief is therefore a heterogeneous catch-all.

Consensus from colleagues 1-3,5:
* Justification without truth is invisible. JF is epistemically good in the justification dimension and subjectively indistinguishable from knowledge, but with K/B only it is filed as mere B. Hence justified false belief collapses into unqualified/unjustified false belief. Justification can only be registered where it coincides with truth, i.e. in K. No distinct state for justified belief.
* Truth without justification is invisible. UT is true but held by luck/guess, not justified, so it is filed as mere B. Hence lucky true belief collapses with JF and UF. Truth is only epistemically marked where it coincides with justification, i.e. in K. No distinct state for lucky true belief.

This is the classic collapse: Belief has to contain justified beliefs and unjustified beliefs, and true beliefs and false beliefs. Knowledge is a proper sub-species K ⊂ B.

Colleague 4 frames the same coarseness differently as a meta-problem for the analysis:
* Justification condition becomes redundant/circular. With only K/B, a justification for a belief can only be a further belief, which is itself either K = JT or mere B. If justification is mere B, JTB collapses to true belief; if justification is K, the analysis is uninformative/circular.
* Truth condition is epistemically inaccessible. From the inside a true belief and a false belief can be equally believed and equally justified; truth is not an epistemic state so K/B cannot guarantee or recognize it.

Unresolved/note: Colleague 4's redundancy/inaccessibility formulation is compatible with the JF/UT collapse described by 1-3,5, just a higher-level diagnosis of why the collapse matters. No substantive disagreement on the two cells that are lost, only on phrasing.

Current working answer: The two non-Gettier problems are the loss of a distinct justified-false-belief state and the loss of a distinct unjustified-true-belief state, i.e. justification is invisible outside truth and truth is invisible outside justification, making Belief heterogeneous and forcing a regress/circularity for justification and unrecognizability for truth.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about the cost of a two-state ontology {Knowledge, Belief} on the JTB analysis K = B & J & T, ignoring Gettier.

Consensus from colleagues 1-3,5: JTB on a binary taxonomy forces a 2×2 truth×justification table into one knowledge cell and one belief catch-all.

* Knowledge = T & J = Justified True Belief.
* Belief = ¬K = J & ~T ∨ ~J & T ∨ ~J & ~T.

That coarse-graining erases independent tracking of justification and truth outside the T&J cell.

Two non-knowledge cells are collapsed:
1. Justification without truth: Justified False Belief, J & ~T & B. Subjectively indistinguishable from knowledge for the believer; epistemically good in the justification dimension but fails truth. With only K/B it must be filed as mere Belief, so it is ontologically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief. Justified false belief is therefore collapsed into unqualified belief; the epistemic value of justification is lost for falsehoods, and Belief becomes heterogeneous containing both epistemically respectable and defective false beliefs.

2. Truth without justification: Unjustified True Belief, ~J & T & B. Epistemically good in the truth dimension only, the paradigm lucky/accidental true belief. With only K/B it must also be filed as mere Belief, so it is indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. The epistemic defect of lack of warrant is lost for truths, and Belief becomes heterogeneous containing both true and false beliefs.

Hence justification is only visible where it coincides with truth, and truth is only epistemically marked where it coincides with justification.

Colleague 4 frames the same coarseness as meta-level problems: with only K/B, justification must be cashed out as either belief or knowledge. If as belief, JTB collapses into true belief; if as knowledge, the definition is circular/uninformative. Truth is not an epistemic state, so from the inside true and false beliefs can be equally believed and equally justified, making the truth condition epistemically inaccessible.

Colleague 5 adds that because there is no distinct justified-belief state, justification must be beliefs about justification, producing the familiar regress/circularity problem: a justified belief is justified by further beliefs which are themselves either K or mere B, with no stopping point.

Unresolved tension: colleagues 1-3,5 describe the problem as the practical collapse of JF and UT into the single Belief category; colleague 4 describes it as redundancy/circularity of the justification clause and inaccessibility of truth. These appear compatible: the collapse follows from the inaccessibility/redundancy under a binary ontology.

My current working view: the two problems the question asks for are the justified-false-belief collapse and the unjustified-true-belief collapse, i.e., Belief has to do the work of three distinct epistemic positions, making justification and truth invisible independently of each other.

1.text:
With a Knowledge / Belief only inventory JTB forces a 2x2 truth × justification space into two labels

* K = J ∧ T ∧ B
* B = ¬K = J ∧ ¬T ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∨ ¬J ∧ ¬T

so the three non-knowledge cells are all filed as the same state B. Belief is therefore a heterogeneous catch-all and K ⊂ B.

That coarsening costs two independent epistemic marks.

1. Justification is invisible outside of truth: justified false belief.
J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is epistemically good in the justification dimension and subjectively indistinguishable from knowledge for the subject who holds it. On JTB it is not K because T fails, so with only K/B it has to be called mere B. Justified false belief is therefore ontologically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B, and from an unjustified true belief ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. There is no distinct justified-belief state. Justification can only be registered where it coincides with truth, i.e. in K, and a justification for a belief can only be cashed out in other beliefs which are themselves either K = JT or mere B. That is the regress / circularity / redundancy problem for the justification clause.

2. Truth is invisible outside of justification: unjustified true belief.
¬J ∧ T ∧ B is true but held by luck, guess or coincidence, not by warrant. On JTB it is not K because J fails, so with only K/B it has to be called mere B. Unjustified true belief is therefore ontologically indistinguishable from justified false belief J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and from unjustified false belief. There is no distinct lucky-true-belief state. Truth can only be epistemically marked where it coincides with justification, i.e. in K. From the inside a true belief and a false belief can be equally believed and equally justified, so truth is epistemically inaccessible / unrecognizable on a K/B taxonomy.

Hence with only Knowledge and Belief you lose a distinct state for justified belief and a distinct state for lucky true belief. Justification is only visible in K and truth is only visible in K, making Belief a mixed class of JF ∨ UT ∨ UF. That is the classic pre-Gettier collapse, the same point Colleague 4 describes as redundancy/circularity of justification and inaccessibility of truth.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the group is converging on the right K/B-specific diagnosis, and we should be careful not to let the regress/circularity issue displace it. Regress and circularity are real worries about justification in general, but they are not the two problems generated by the restriction to only Knowledge and Belief. They are downstream of a more basic taxonomy failure.

With only K and B available, JTB gives us:

- K = justified true belief.
- B = everything else.

That means the non-knowledge cells are forced into one undifferentiated state, B:

- Justified false belief: J & ~T
- Unjustified true belief: ~J & T
- Unjustified false belief: ~J & ~T

So the two problems are:

1. **Justified false belief collapses into mere Belief.**  
   A belief can be well justified and still false. JTB cannot call it Knowledge because truth fails, so under a K/B-only scheme it is just B. But then it becomes indistinguishable from an irrational or baseless false belief. Justification outside the true case has no separate epistemic status.

2. **Unjustified true belief collapses into mere Belief.**  
   A belief can be true merely by luck or accident and still lack justification. JTB cannot call it Knowledge because justification fails, so under a K/B-only scheme it is also just B. But then it becomes indistinguishable from false belief, and the fact that it is true is epistemically invisible.

With a binary inventory K / B the JTB analysis forces

K p  ↔  B p ∧ J p ∧ T p
B p  ↔  ¬K p

i.e.  B = J & ~T ∨ ~J & T ∨ ~J & ~T

so the 2×2 truth × justification matrix is coarse-grained into one factive good cell and one catch-all non-knowledge cell. Justification and truth can only be registered together in the T&J cell.

That coarse-graining makes Belief heterogeneous and erases the independent tracking of J and T outside of K.

It is epistemically good in the justification dimension and subjectively indistinguishable from knowledge for the believer, but on JTB it is not K because T fails. With only K / B it has to be filed as mere Belief. Belief therefore has to contain both epistemically respectable false beliefs and epistemically defective false beliefs. Justified false belief is ontologically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief, so the value of justification is lost for falsehoods and justification is only visible where it coincides with truth.

* Truth without justification.  ~J p & T p & B p: an unjustified true belief, the paradigm lucky/accidental true belief. It is epistemically good only in the truth dimension, but on JTB it is not K because J fails. With only K / B it also has to be filed as mere Belief. Belief therefore has to contain true beliefs as well as false beliefs. An unjustified true belief is ontologically indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief, so the defect of lack of warrant is lost for truths and truth is only epistemically marked where it coincides with justification.

* T & ~J = UT
* ~T & J = JF
* ~T & ~J = UF

The question is the cost of JTB under a strict Knowledge/Belief binary ontology, Gettier excluded.

Core structure: JTB gives four logical cells T×J:
* T&J = JT = Knowledge
* T&~J = UT = unjustified true belief
* ~T&J = JF = justified false belief
* ~T&~J = UF = unjustised false belief
With only K/B labels, K = J∧T∧B and B = ¬K = JF ∨ UT ∨ UF. Hence K ⊂ B and Belief is a heterogeneous catch-all.

Current consensus after round 3:
* Justification without truth is invisible. JF = J∧~T∧B is epistemically good in justification and subjectively indistinguishable from knowledge for holder, but fails T so JTB cannot call it K. With only K/B it is filed as mere B, ontologically indistinguishable from UF and UT. Therefore justified false belief collapses into mere Belief, justification can only be registered where it coincides with truth i.e. in K, and there is no distinct justified-belief state. This is the justification-mismatch / justification invisible outside truth problem.

With only K/B it is filed as mere B, ontologically indistinguishable from JF and UF.
